product_overview: Execution runtime for ForgeGraph: a Go gRPC service that validates workflow graphs, executes nodes concurrently, emits execution events for the backend to persist, and exposes Prometheus metrics.
core_goals: Accept run-control requests over gRPC for ping, start, status, and cancellation.
Validate graphs and compute execution plans before runtime processing begins.
Execute workflow node types including prompt, tool, transform, merge, branch, human-gate, output, subgraph, and observation nodes.
Coordinate execution adapters such as memory access, tool manifests, and runtime telemetry without becoming the durable source of truth.
Expose operational metrics and support deterministic testing of runtime and adapter behavior.

features.name: Engine gRPC Run Control
features.description: Core gRPC interface for health, run startup, status lookup, and cancellation.
user_flows: GET /ready -> Receive 200 readiness payload with grpc_ready=true
Native gRPC StartRun/GetRunStatus/CancelRun behavior is exercised through engine integration tests or backend-owned control-plane flows, not JSON-over-HTTP endpoints
Unknown HTTP paths should not masquerade as gRPC run-control APIs

features.name: Graph Validation and Planning
features.description: Domain services validate graph payloads, evaluate conditions, and compute execution order and token budgets before execution.
user_flows: GET /ready -> Receive 200 readiness payload before native gRPC graph validation is exercised
Invalid graph rejection is verified by backend graph validation and native gRPC integration tests, not REST-shaped TestSprite calls

features.name: Node Execution Runtime
features.description: Executors implement runtime behavior for prompt, tool, transform, branch, merge, output, subgraph, human-gate, and observation nodes.
user_flows: Backend-owned run APIs create durable run state, while the engine executes ephemeral work and emits callbacks
GET /metrics -> Receive 200 Prometheus metrics text for runtime observability

features.name: Persistence, Memory, and Tooling Adapters
features.description: Runtime adapters provide ephemeral execution dependencies such as repositories, Redis and PostgreSQL stores, credential resolution, marketplace manifest refresh, and tool registry support.
user_flows: GET /ready -> Receive 200 readiness payload with grpc_ready=true when engine dependencies are initialized

features.name: Execution Events and Observability
features.description: The engine emits execution events for the backend control plane, records metrics/traces, and supports runtime observability hooks.
user_flows: Backend-owned run control invokes native gRPC and engine event delivery emits callbacks for backend persistence
GET /metrics -> Receive 200 metrics output including runtime telemetry

known_limitations.issue: Most externally visible behavior is mediated through gRPC calls and asynchronous callbacks rather than a broad HTTP API.
known_limitations.impact: Test tooling that assumes REST-style endpoints must adapt to gRPC semantics or use the metrics endpoint for HTTP checks.

known_limitations.issue: Full execution paths can depend on external databases, Redis, callback endpoints, and model or provider integrations.
known_limitations.impact: Integration tests need mocks or supporting services to cover production-like behavior reliably.
